truthPage.title: The truth about epilepsy
truthPage.intro: Explore reliable information, challenge misconceptions, and learn seizure first aid.

contagious.truth: Epilepsy is not contagious. It is a neurological condition and cannot be transmitted from one person to another.

work.truth: Many people living with epilepsy work and lead active lives. Needs vary from person to person and with their health.

mouth.myth: You should put something in a person's mouth during a seizure.
mouth.truth: Never put anything in the person's mouth; it could cause injury. Clear nearby hazards and protect their head.

mental.truth: Epilepsy is a neurological condition related to brain activity; it is not, in itself, a mental illness.

prevalence.title: Global prevalence

control.title: Effective treatment
control.description: Up to 70% of people living with epilepsy could become seizure-free with appropriate diagnosis and treatment.

causes.title: Many possible causes
causes.description: Epilepsy can have different causes, including brain injury, infection, stroke, genetic factors, and others.

treatment.title: Individualized care
treatment.description: Antiseizure medicines can control seizures for many people. Treatment should be managed with a healthcare professional.

truthPage.firstAidTitle: What to do during a seizure
truthPage.firstAidIntro: First aid guidance for a convulsive seizure.

steps.1: Stay calm and time how long the seizure lasts.
steps.2: Move dangerous objects away and protect the person from injury.
steps.3: Place something soft and flat under their head.
steps.4: Loosen tight clothing around the neck and, if possible, gently turn the person onto their side when the jerking stops.
steps.5: Stay with the person and reassure them as they regain awareness.
steps.6: Call emergency services if the seizure lasts 5 minutes or longer, another seizure follows, the person is injured, or they do not regain awareness.

doNotItems.1: Do not put anything in their mouth.
doNotItems.3: Do not give water, food, or medicine until they are fully alert.
doNotItems.4: Do not leave the person alone after the seizure.

truthPage.emergencyCallout: Call local emergency services for a prolonged seizure, repeated seizures, or breathing difficulty.
truthPage.firstAidNote: This guidance does not replace first-aid training or advice from a healthcare professional.

gdpr.pageIntro: Understand the GDPR, the data involved, and the rights people have on Move4Epilepsy.
gdpr.introTitle: Your data tells a personal story. Protecting it matters.
gdpr.introText: This page explains what the GDPR is, why it matters especially on a platform dealing with epilepsy and treatment, which data categories the API separate from the frontend provides for, and what rights you may exercise. It complements the privacy policy; it does not replace it.
gdpr.whatText: The General Data Protection Regulation (EU Regulation 2016/679) governs the use of information relating to an identifiable person. It has applied in the European Union since 25 May 2018 and may also apply to organizations outside the EU depending on their activities involving people in the EU. Applicable rules must be checked for each country and context.
gdpr.scopeNote: Data can still be personal even when a form is submitted without an account or under a pseudonym: a combination of age, location, treatment, and a personal account may sometimes identify someone. Health data receives enhanced protection.
gdpr.whyTitle: Why does this matter especially here?
gdpr.whyText: Information about epilepsy, medication, side effects, cost, or access can be highly private. Responsible collection helps people understand what they share, reduces exposure risks, and makes it possible to use aggregated data to study access inequalities without publishing individual stories.

principles.lawfulnessText: Every use must have a documented legal basis. Health data also requires a specific condition, including under Article 9 of the GDPR; this cannot be inferred from the API code alone.
principles.purposeText: Data should serve explained purposes, such as handling a request, responding to an alert, or studying access to treatment, and should not be reused incompatibly.
principles.minimizationText: Ask only for information needed for the stated service. Optional fields and free-text accounts need particular care because they may contain identifying details.
principles.accuracyText: People should be able to correct inaccurate data, and conclusions should account for the limits and representativeness of submitted reports.
principles.retentionText: Set a justified retention period and explain what happens afterwards: deletion, anonymization, or permitted archiving.
principles.securityText: Restrict access, protect communications and systems, prevent disclosures, and plan how to respond to an incident.

gdpr.dataTitle: What data does the API provide for?
gdpr.dataIntro: The categories below come from the API models and forms. The API is developed separately from the Vue frontend. They describe possible fields, not proof that every field is collected by this frontend or retained in production.

data.healthText: Age, sex, location, medication, dosage, frequency, treatment dates or duration, cost, effectiveness, side effects, difficulties, availability, alternatives, and comments. The treatment submission route can be used without an account; this data remains sensitive and is not necessarily anonymous.
data.locationText: Country or locality, medication searched for, and result information. The search model also provides fields for IP address and browser (user-agent); whether they are populated and how long they are retained must be verified.
data.contactText: A medicine availability alert may include an email address or phone number linked to a medicine and geographic area. Partnership applications may include a person's name, organization, contact details, and address.
data.contributionText: Reviews, ratings, and free text; medicine and pharmacy reports, prices, availability, and possibly the reporter's name or phone number; and answers to questions about perceptions of epilepsy.
data.technicalText: Account models provide for email, username, role, and profile. The server logs requests (method, path, and status); hosting configuration and actual logs must be checked before specifying which traces are retained.

gdpr.technicalCaveat: The API sets a 30-day expiry for a search alert. An expiry or deactivation alone does not establish that data is actually deleted: purging, backups, and actual retention periods must be confirmed.
gdpr.purposesText: The visible features and API routes indicate possible purposes: recording treatment experiences, receiving reviews and reports, managing medicine availability alerts, handling partnership requests, operating professional accounts, and producing analyses of medicine access. The exact purpose, legal basis, and necessary data should be specified for each form before collection. Analyses should favor aggregated results and avoid publishing information that could identify someone.
gdpr.rightsIntro: Where the GDPR applies, you may notably ask the data controller to:

rights.access: Access your data and receive information about how it is used.
rights.rectification: Have inaccurate or incomplete data corrected.
rights.erasure: Request erasure in situations provided for by law.
rights.objection: Object to certain processing based on legitimate interests or a public task.
rights.portability: Receive certain data you provided, subject to the conditions for data portability.
rights.withdrawal: Withdraw consent where processing relies on it, without affecting earlier processing.
rights.complaint: Lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority.

gdpr.rightsLimit: Not every right applies in every situation, and legal exceptions exist. Health data also requires a specific legal basis and processing condition. To exercise a right, contact the controller; its identity and official contact details should be clearly published.
gdpr.knownTitle: What we know — and what still needs clarification
gdpr.knownText: Reviewing the API code identifies fields, public forms, accounts, and access restricted to certain roles. This is not enough to demonstrate the compliance of the entire service or establish its hosting practices.
gdpr.implementationTitle: Current state of the Vue frontend
gdpr.implementationIntro: The information below describes forms in this Vue version. It should not be confused with capabilities planned for the separate API or requirements that still need implementation.
gdpr.implementationCurrentText: The Vue form collects, among other things, age, sex, location, treatment information, and access experience. The availability-alert option is optional. At present, this journey does not request an email address for the treatment submission, show an explicit consent checkbox, or verify an address. A review screen is present, but it displays only some answers before submission. The frontend does not yet offer self-service viewing, editing, or deletion of these submissions.
gdpr.implementationPlannedText: Verified email, a two-step consent flow with a versioned record, alerts, and later management of submissions are documented requirements, not features currently available in this form. The proposed journey and API contract must be validated by the backend team and data controller before integration and production use.
gdpr.toConfirmText: The controller's legal identity and address; purposes and legal bases, including the condition applicable to health data; recipients and processors; hosting locations and transfers outside the country; exact retention periods and backup purging; procedures for exercising rights; and the contact details of a data protection officer, if there is one.
gdpr.disclaimer: This page is an educational explanation based on the code reviewed, not legal advice or a compliance statement. It does not replace a complete privacy policy validated by the data controller and tailored to the countries where the service is offered.
gdpr.contactTitle: Questions or requests about your data?
gdpr.contactText: You can write to the contact address currently published on the portal. This is a general contact point; it does not by itself confirm the legal identity of the data controller.

cancel.answer: Cancellation terms must be available before subscribing. Self-service cancellation is not currently enabled.

networkPlan.question: How does the Network offer work?
networkPlan.answer: It is intended for organizations managing several pharmacies. Pricing and terms will depend on the number of sites, needs, and market.

privacy.question: How is my information protected?
privacy.answer: Professional data must be handled under applicable privacy rules. Patient health information is not intended to be exposed to pharmacies.

unsupportedMarket.question: What if my country is not listed?
unsupportedMarket.answer: Contact the team with your country and needs. No listed price means no offer is currently configured for that market.

subscriptions.quoteTitle: A quote tailored to your organization
subscriptions.quoteDescription: Tell us your billing country, the number of locations, and your professional needs. The team can respond based on available offers.
subscriptions.quotePrivacyNote: Do not include any health information in this request.
subscriptions.quoteMailNotice: This request opens your email application and is not stored on the platform.
subscriptions.finalDescription: Build your pharmacy's presence on a platform designed to make useful information easier to find.

servicesSearch.title: Find services
servicesSearch.intro: Browse pharmacies registered on the platform. Availability information should be confirmed directly with each pharmacy.
servicesSearch.hospitalsUnavailable: There is no verified hospital directory connected to the platform yet. Check local resources or contact a healthcare professional.
servicesSearch.disclaimer: Pharmacy information may be out of date. Call ahead and confirm your medication is available before travelling.
